title: Dearness Allowance Demands: Understanding the Call for Inflation-Linked Pay

faq.a: Dearness Allowance is a component of salary paid by the government to its employees and pensioners. It is designed to offset the impact of inflation and protect their purchasing power against rising costs of living.

faq.q: Who is eligible for Dearness Allowance?
faq.a: Central and state government employees, as well as pensioners, are eligible for Dearness Allowance. The rates and calculation methods might vary slightly between central and state governments.

DA is typically revised twice a year by the Central Government, usually effective from January 1st and July 1st. The revisions are based on the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) data.

Yes, Dearness Allowance is fully taxable under the head "Salaries" as per the Income Tax Act. It is included in the gross salary for tax calculation purposes (refer to Income Tax India: https://incometax.gov.in).

faq.q: What is the significance of a DA merger with basic pay?
faq.a: A DA merger with basic pay means that the DA component becomes part of the basic salary. This increases the base for calculating other allowances (like HRA, TA) and retirement benefits (like gratuity and pension), significantly boosting an employee's overall compensation and post-retirement security.

faq.q: What is the Old Pension Scheme (OPS) being demanded?
faq.a: The Old Pension Scheme (OPS) offered a defined benefit pension, where employees received a fixed percentage of their last drawn salary as pension. It is being demanded by some groups as an alternative to the National Pension System (NPS), citing better retirement security.
